item.title: Senegal’s Saint-Louis Regatta keeps centuries of tradition alive
item.description: In Saint-Louis, Senegal, traditional pirogue races are keeping alive a centuries-old tradition dating back nearly 200 years. Held in the fishing district of Guet Ndar, the 3.5-kilometre race brings together dozens of rowers and huge crowds, turning the event into both a major sporting competition and a celebration of local culture. But despite the race's popularity and the money it generates, competitors are not paid and are calling for greater recognition for the sport. Publicado también por: France 24 - English. Fuente: Al Jazeera English.

item.title: In 1988, an English farmer stopped cultivating his entire 377-acre wheat farm
item.description: An abandoned wheat farm in England has been transformed into a thriving nature reserve after decades of neglect. Following a dedicated public campaign, £1.5 million was raised to acquire the land, ensuring its protection for future generations. This 377-acre area now boasts a rich variety of wildlife, including numerous endangered bird species, and will be overseen by the Wildlife Trust as a cherished habitat. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
